assumptions: Public KSeF interfaces permit a useful least-privilege monitoring workflow.
The service begins read-only with human-approved remediation.
Accounting offices experience heterogeneous exceptions not already resolved adequately by their primary software.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Production pilots with two or more offices documenting exception frequency, labor saved, acceptable credentialing and security, paid conversion, low support minutes per client, and retention despite incumbent software improvements.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Mandatory structured invoicing creates a narrow, measurable exception queue across many clients that can be automated and operationally managed.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Bookkeeper rework and payment delays are credible current costs, but exception incidence, hours saved, and willingness to pay have not been measured.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Setup fees and prepaid subscriptions can support good cash conversion and software-like margins, but human escalation, security, liability, churn, and CAC may materially reduce the modeled economics.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Independent Polish accounting offices managing many SMEs are a precise, economically meaningful beachhead with concentrated recurring workflow.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A specialist may move faster on cross-client operations, yet accounting-suite vendors control embedded workflows and can bundle equivalent dashboards.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted exception position can expand into reconciliation, payment status, VAT workflow, client controls, and other Polish finance-compliance operations.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Resolution patterns and workflow integration can compound, but customer permissions are revocable and an anonymized playbook is likely reproducible by incumbents.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Multi-client monitoring, guided resolution, and SLA evidence could materially reduce labor versus free access tools, but superiority over upgraded accounting suites is unproven.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Mandatory KSeF adoption is already creating a sharp transition period in which offices must establish reliable new operating routines.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Accounting offices are identifiable and ERP referrals are plausible, but the founder holds no office relationship, credential access, or distribution agreement.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A read-only monitor is feasible within budget and part-time constraints, while production security, tax-process liability, credentials, and support responsiveness demand disciplined specialist oversight.

highest_value_structural_change: Obtain a channel or embedded integration with an accounting-software implementer while standardizing a read-only, least-privilege exception feed across offices.
main_structural_strength: A regulation-driven, recurring and measurable operational queue offers a narrow automation wedge with clear before-and-after labor metrics.
primary_score_limiter: The likely incumbent bundling response and unknown exception workload make durable willingness to pay uncertain.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The Ministry supplies free KSeF applications, and large accounting platforms are natural owners of exception handling.
